key_insight: PathFM goes beyond predicting separate future values and instead learns full multivariate trajectory dependence, making forecasts useful for quantities that depend on the whole path, like peaks, totals, and timing. It uses flow matching to generate realistic future paths quickly.
problem_solved: Most forecasting foundation models only predict marginal quantiles, which hides how future time points depend on each other. This paper addresses the need to model full trajectory structure for downstream tasks where the shape of the forecast path matters.
method: Introduces PathFM, a trajectory-based forecasting model for multivariate time series.
Uses flow matching to generate future paths directly, capturing dependence across time and variables.
Aims to produce fast generative forecasts rather than only marginal prediction intervals.
impact: For practitioners, PathFM can improve forecasts for decisions that depend on the entire future path, not just point estimates. This is especially useful in energy, demand planning, operations, and any setting where peak values, cumulative effects, or event timing matter.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram comparing marginal quantile forecasts vs full trajectory generation
Flow matching pipeline showing history input to generated future paths
Example multivariate time-series plot with several plausible forecast trajectories
Icons for peak load, cumulative demand, and event timing to highlight downstream use cases
paper_title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
paper_authors: Jiachen Yao, Xiyuan Zhang, Annan Yu, Boran Han, Abdul Fatir Ansari
